\title{On the Convergence Properties of Stochastic Gradient Methods}
\author{J. Smith \and A. Chen}
\date{March 2024}

\begin{document}

\maketitle

\section{Introduction}

Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) has become the dominant optimization method
for training large-scale machine learning models. In this paper, we analyze the
convergence behavior of SGD under relaxed smoothness assumptions and provide
tighter bounds for the non-convex setting.

Let $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ denote the objective function we wish
to minimize. We assume access to an unbiased gradient oracle that returns
$g(x, \xi)$ such that $\mathbb{E}[g(x, \xi)] = \nabla f(x)$.

\section{Preliminaries}

\textbf{Definition 1.} A function $f$ is $L$-smooth if for all $x, y$:
\begin{equation}
  \|\nabla f(x) - \nabla f(y)\| \leq L \|x - y\|
\end{equation}

We further assume bounded variance of the stochastic gradients:
\begin{equation}
  \mathbb{E}\left[\|g(x, \xi) - \nabla f(x)\|^2\right] \leq \sigma^2
\end{equation}

\section{Main Results}

\textbf{Theorem 1.} Under Assumptions 1--3, running SGD with step size
$\eta_t = \frac{c}{\sqrt{T}}$ for $T$ iterations yields:
\begin{equation}
  \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} \mathbb{E}\|\nabla f(x_t)\|^2
  \leq \frac{2(f(x_0) - f^*)}{\sqrt{T}} + \frac{L\sigma^2}{\sqrt{T}}
\end{equation}

This result improves upon the classical bound by a factor of $\log T$ in the
dominant term. The proof relies on a novel recursive decomposition of the
gradient norm, which we detail in Section~4.
